text:
Charlie Coyle had his night on Nov. 3: two goals and two assists as Columbus beat Colorado 7-2, against the team he played 19 games for. RotoWire called it a "Massive revenge game against Avs." That night accounts for two of his three goals this season.

Look past the box score, though, and he's one of the Blue Jackets' best drivers of play. Columbus gets 56.5% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, 11.7 points better than without him, and his ice time has climbed to 20.7 minutes over his last ten games.

The goals just haven't matched it. He has 3 on 4.4 expected, and our wins-added measure has him 490th of 506 skaters because his goals haven't come in moments that swung games. That is mostly timing, not talent. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 90th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season. At 34, with 13 points in 15 games, he is doing the job. The scoreboard is a step behind.
headline: Coyle's numbers are better than his luck
